lines.en: Martin, Martin, Martin, Martin, that is my favorite show, man.
That is so great. Shenanay and the...
Oh, man.
My muscles are so sore.
From karate.
Usually, when people find out about the prison thing,
they get pretty weird.
So, you all want to know what I was in for?
No, that's not cool.
You don't have to tell them.
I really don't mind. It was a stupid mistake.
I was working in finance,
and I got involved in some insider trading.
So, I spent a little time in the clink.
That is awesome.
I had Martin explain to me three times
what he got arrested for,
because...
it sounds an awful lot like what I do here every day.
Oh, yeah. I was in prison.
That's where I got the name Creed.
I was arrested once for loitering outside of Dunkin' Donuts.
I am not the luckiest guy in the world.
Have you ever heard of Pruno?
It's a wine made from fruit and sugar and ketchup we used to make in the toilets in prison.
Man, I miss that stuff.
What was prison like?
It's not terrible, boring. We do the same thing every day.
But at least we get outdoors time.
You got outdoors time?
Two hours every day.
Sometimes we play pick-up football games.
Michael, why don't we get outdoors time?
Yeah, some days I never go outside.
Well, we are running a business.
What was your cell like?
Not good.
It's a little bit bigger than Michael's office.
But I really only slept there during the day. Our time was our own. They had classes. I took some watercolor classes.
They have art classes?
Yeah.
They have business classes there?
They did, taught by some Harvard Business School guys. A lot of the guys also that were in the class, the inmates, a lot of them have gone on to do extraordinary things in the business.
Kind of sounds like prison's better than Thunder Mifflin.
Oh, okay, well, that's not true.
I would so rather be in prison.
Prison sounds great.
No, you would not.
This place is not prison. This place -- It's way better than prison.
That went better than I thought.
Would have gone better if you had never been to prison.
I would be this upset if I found out anyone in this office had committed a crime.
But come on, Martin. There are two black men in this office and one has done time. What the hell was he thinking?
Hey, you like working here, right?
Please. Is the Pope German? I want to run a background check on the convict.
Okay, you have to relax because he was in jail for insider trading.
Yes, that is what the convict said. The convict said that he, the convict, Reed, liar, was in jail for the harmless crime of insider trading.
Which is exactly what a convict would say.
Stop it.
What if he hurts someone?
He's not --
Do you want that on your conscience?
Oh.
Just let me look in his HR file.
We can't do that. That is unconstitutional.
Constitutions are made to be broken.
All right, just stop it. I'm going -- I'm going to punch you in the tooth. You have to stop.
I think I would do well in prison. Prison is all about establishing dominance, which is one of my fortes.
On the first day, I would go up to the meanest guy there and I would point right at him and say,
"Not today, friend." And then I'd give him one of these.
Score!
Two for flinching.
